mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p>0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by >0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over the prior quarter indicates a restrictive monetary policy with falling inflation, which historically correlates with positive risk asset returns as growth concerns subside but rates remain high, driving S&P 500 gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month drop in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals a collapse in residential construction activity, which reduces demand for materials and related equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST drops >10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS shows accelerating growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive quarters signals synchronized demand expansion, which increases earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both rise for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise for two consecutive quarters.
